title: The Berlin Bear - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has a bear because of its name.** The name is most likely Slavic for swamp, but to German ears it sounds like Bär, so the town took a bear for its arms.
**The first bears appear on the city seal of 1280,** standing beside the Brandenburg eagle. The bear took the centre over the next two centuries.
**Today's coat of arms:** an upright black bear with red tongue and claws on a silver shield under a crown, official since 1954 in the West and 1991 for all Berlin.
**Best free bear: the old bear pit in Köllnischer Park.** Real bears lived there from 1939 to 2015; it is now a free art space, open daily 10:00 to 18:00.
**Two minutes from Museum Island:** the Bärenbrunnen on Werderscher Markt, a 1928 fountain of a mother bear and her cubs.
**Buddy Bears are everywhere.** Photograph the ones you pass; do not plan a day around them.
**Knut the polar bear** stands in the Museum für Naturkunde, closed on Mondays. Go for the dinosaurs as well.
